title: The kernel of abelian-quotient Picard pullback is algebraically trivial
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $A/F$ be an abelian variety [def-sc-abelian-variety], and let $G/F$ be a smooth separated commutative group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Let $r\geq0$ and suppose $q:G\to A$ fits into an exact sequence of fppf sheaves $1\to\mathbf G_{m,F}^r\to G\xrightarrow{q}A\to1$ [def-pc-fppf-site], where $\mathbf G_{m,F}=\operatorname{Spec}F[t,t^{-1}]$ with multiplication. Exactness means the first map identifies its source with the kernel and every section of $A$ lifts fppf locally to $G$. If $N$ is an invertible $\mathcal O_A$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] and $q^*N\simeq\mathcal O_G$ [def-pc-module-pullback], then $N$ is algebraically equivalent to $\mathcal O_A$. Algebraic equivalence is the equivalence relation on invertible-module isomorphism classes generated by two fibres of a family of invertible modules on $A\times_FV$, with $V$ a smooth connected separated finite-type $F$-scheme [def-pc-fibre-product]; tensor products and duals give the group law and inverse [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

source.place: I Proposition 9.3, printed pp.41--42: extensions of an abelian variety by G_m and Pic^0. Agent-extracted consequence for the kernel of pullback along a split-torus extension, using character pushouts; not claimed as the verbatim statement of Proposition 9.3.

proof.text: Write $T=\mathbf G_m^r$ and $i:T\to G$ for the kernel inclusion. On any fppf cover where a section $a$ of $A$ has a lift $g$, the map $t\mapsto g\,i(t)$ identifies its fibre with $T$: its inverse sends a second lift $h$ to the unique $t$ with $i(t)=g^{-1}h$. These formulas are inverse on all test schemes, so $G\to A$ is a locally trivial $T$-torsor. The torus-smoothness statement makes $T$ smooth; its coordinate presentation $F[t_1,z_1,\ldots,t_r,z_r]/(t_1z_1-1,\ldots,t_rz_r-1)$ makes it affine and finitely presented. The affine smooth torsor-representability statement applied over $A$ gives that $q$ is affine, smooth and surjective and that $(g,t)\mapsto(g,g\,i(t))$ identifies $G\times_FT$ with $G\times_AG$. Smoothness gives flatness and local finite presentation; thus $\{q\}$ is an fppf covering and hence an fpqc covering. The abelian-variety characterization gives geometric integrality of $A$, hence geometric connectedness. Its commutativity also follows by lifting two sections locally to the commutative group $G$. The semiabelian-power-integrality statement with $n=1$ now gives that $G$ is integral.

source.place: I Proposition 9.3, pp.41--42, character-pushout application; torsor preparation from Stacks groupoids.tex Tag 049C (remark-fun-with-torsors). Agent argument.

proof.text: Choose a frame $s:\mathcal O_G\xrightarrow{\sim}q^*N$, using the assumed triviality. Since $q(g\,i(t))=q(g)$, there is a unique regular unit $u$ on $G\times_FT$ with $s(g\,i(t))=u(g,t)s(g)$, and $u(g,1)=1$. The torus is integral: its Laurent polynomial coordinate ring embeds in $F(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$, so is a domain; for $r=0$ its coordinate ring is $F$. Both $G$ and $T$ are nonempty integral separated finite-type $F$-schemes, with identity $F$-points. Rosenlicht's normalized identity with basepoints $(1,1)$ gives $u(g,t)=u(g,1)u(1,t)u(1,1)^{-1}=u(1,t)$. Put $\chi(t)=u(1,t)$. Comparing $s(g\,i(t_1t_2))$ with $s((g\,i(t_1))i(t_2))$ gives $\chi(t_1t_2)=\chi(t_2)\chi(t_1)$, and $\chi(1)=1$. These are identities of regular functions on products, so $\chi:T\to\mathbf G_m$ is a group-scheme homomorphism, including on nonreduced test schemes.

source.place: Character of a pulled-back frame: agent argument using literature/milne-algebraic-groups_iAG2017.pdf, Proposition 12.48, identity (79), pp.246--247.

proof.text: Apply the character-pushout statement to $1\to T\to G\to A\to1$ and $\chi$. It gives a commutative group extension $1\to\mathbf G_m\to E_\chi\to A\to1$, an invertible module $M_\chi$ whose frame torsor is $E_\chi$, and a frame $\sigma_\chi$ of $q^*M_\chi$ with $\sigma_\chi(g\,i(t))=\chi(t)\sigma_\chi(g)$. The sign convention is fixed by the quotient relation $(g,z)\sim(g\,i(t),\chi(t)^{-1}z)$, which gives $[g\,i(t),1]=[g,\chi(t)]$.

source.place: I Proposition 9.3, pp.41--42: form the character pushout before applying the classification; its represented construction is the cited prerequisite.

proof.text: Let $\varphi:q^*N\xrightarrow{\sim}q^*M_\chi$ send $s$ to $\sigma_\chi$. On $G\times_AG\simeq G\times_FT$, both frames at the second lift $g\,i(t)$ equal $\chi(t)$ times their frames at $g$. Thus the two pullbacks of $\varphi$ agree under the canonical descent identifications: applying either map to $s(g\,i(t))=\chi(t)s(g)$ gives $\chi(t)\sigma_\chi(g)=\sigma_\chi(g\,i(t))$. Full faithfulness of fpqc descent along the covering $q$ descends $\varphi$ to $N\to M_\chi$. The same compatibility for $\varphi^{-1}$ descends the inverse; their composites are identities because their pullbacks are. Hence $N\simeq M_\chi$.

source.place: Stacks descent.tex Tag 023T (proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent), full faithfulness; applied to the displayed frame calculation.

proof.text: Let $a\in A(F)$. The fibre of $E_\chi\simeq M_\chi^\times$ over $a$ consists of the frames of the one-dimensional $F$-vector space $a^*M_\chi$, so it has an $F$-point $e$. Right multiplication $x\mapsto xe$ on $E_\chi$ lies over the translation $t_a$, because $E_\chi\to A$ is a homomorphism, and it commutes with the $\mathbf G_m$-action, which by the character-pushout statement is multiplication by $[1,z]$ in the commutative group $E_\chi$. Transported through $E_\chi\simeq M_\chi^\times$, it sends a frame $f$ of $M_\chi|_U$, for a Zariski open $U\subseteq A$, to a frame $\psi(f)$ of $(t_a^*M_\chi)|_U$ with $\psi(cf)=c\psi(f)$ for units $c$. Hence $cf\mapsto c\psi(f)$, $c\in\mathcal O_U$, does not depend on the frame $f$, and these maps glue to an isomorphism $M_\chi\simeq t_a^*M_\chi$. Thus $t_a^*M_\chi\cong M_\chi$ for every $a\in A(F)$, and the homogeneous-line statement gives that $M_\chi$ is algebraically equivalent to $\mathcal O_A$; its smooth connected parameter varieties are the item's smooth connected separated finite-type parameter schemes. Substituting the isomorphism $N\simeq M_\chi$ of step 4 gives the conclusion. For $r=0$, $\chi$ is trivial, $E_\chi=A\times\mathbf G_m$ and $M_\chi\simeq\mathcal O_A$.
